newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks firm at midday as rate pressures ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm at midday as rate pressures ease.

text.p: Wall Street stocks tallied solid gains at midday, aided by lower interest rates and optimism about the outlook for inflation and corporate earnings.

The Dow industrials were up 40 points, or 0.6 percent, to 6750 at midday, just a trace off the index's high for the day. The Nasdaq Composite turned in an even better performance, gaining 12 points, or 0.9 percent, to 1343.
Stocks were boosted primarily by a bond market rally sparked by a lower-than-expected rise in the U.S. Consumer Price Index.
The Labor Department reported CPI rose 0.3 percent in December, in line with forecasts.

More important, said analysts, was a surprisingly small increase when volatile food and energy prices were excluded. The so-called "core" CPI rose only 0.1 percent, a smaller gain than economists had forecast.
"The CPI looks like a clear signal things are on the right track and appears to have relaxed interest rate concerns," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 27/32, pushing the yield down to 6.78 percent.
While lower rates were clearly helping stocks, analysts said they preferred to see more progress before calling the rate picture a favorable one.

"I think we could see a rally past 6.75 percent and I think that's a threshold level," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "If we don't get throught 6.75 percent, we're at extreme risk that one bad number could get us all the way to seven percent."
Shortly after midday, gains on the Dow industrials widened past the 50-point mark, triggering the New York Stock Exchange's index-arbitrage program trading curbs at 1218 EST/1718 GMT.
Financial stocks were among the strongest performers of the morning, helped by strong early returns on the earnings front and the improved interest rate picture.
Techs were also solid, led by chip bellwether Intel Corp, which is due to report earnings after the close.
"Intel hasn't disappointed in a long time," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.

Also higher was chip maker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. It received a vote of confidence early in the day when SoundView Financial started coverage of the company with a short-term buy rating. Shares jumped four to 33.

Shares in health maintenance organizations were weaker on fears the U.S. would move to slow premium growth rates. Oxford Health Plans Inc fell 2-3/4 to 52-5/8 and United Healthcare Corp lost one to 43-1/4.
Payless ShoeSource Inc jumped 2-1/2 to 37-1/8. The company announced it would acquire J. Baker Inc's Parade of Shoes unit. Terms were not disclosed.
"The retail sales numbers confirm that the consumer came back solidly in the fourth quarter," agreed Bankers Trust managing director and chief global markets economist John Williams.
Williams said if that momentum carries forward into 1997, inflation pressures will continue to build and eventually will show up in the CPI.

"That's why we think that if the Federal Reserve sees some upward pressure on the CPI and also in the Employment Cost Index due on January 28, it will tighten (monetary policy) in the spring," he said.
